name: Biocon Ltd
title: Biocon Ltd - 532523 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Biocon Q2 FY27 revenue deferral of ~5% (~$20m) from biosimilars shifted to October; management reiterates stronger H2 and mid-20s biosimilar margins, but Syngene guidance not repeated.

summary.headline: Biocon Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 2% YoY with EBITDA at INR865 crore; ~5% biosimilar revenue (~$20m) slipped into October, lifting H2 expectations.
summary.overview: Consolidated operating revenue grew 2% YoY in Q2 FY27, with biosimilars up 5% YoY and Syngene services up 13% QoQ. Consolidated EBITDA was INR865 crore, helped by a sharp Generics margin recovery and Syngene's sequential improvement. Management attributed a one-off deferral of about 5% of quarter revenue in biosimilars (logistics and geopolitical issues, mainly insulin and mAbs) to October, and guided H2 to be stronger than H1. Reported net profit before exceptionals was INR44 crore, and interest cost fell 12% YoY to INR240 crore.

segments.name: Biosimilars
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR2,809 crore and EBITDA INR623 crore, with R&D at 7% of revenue; H1 revenue grew 9% YoY and H1 EBITDA margin was 24%. Quarter hit by about 5% (~$20m, roughly INR135-138 crore) one-off deferral, booked in October.

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR774 crore, up YoY, with EBITDA of INR64 crore (8% margin) versus INR7 crore a year ago. H1 revenue grew 15% YoY and H1 EBITDA was INR120 crore against a loss of INR28 crore in H1 FY26.

segments.name: Services (Syngene)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR833 crore, up 13% QoQ, with EBITDA INR175 crore (20% margin vs 15% in Q1). H1 revenue INR1,569 crore and EBITDA INR291 crore; FY27 remains a transition year due to reduced demand from a large biologics client.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1 across biosimilars, Generics profitability and Syngene recovery.
Biosimilars EBITDA margin expected in the mid-20s, improving as revenue scales; management is holding full-year margin view of about 25%.
Management expects strong double-digit dollar growth in H2 for biosimilars; rupee reporting may add upside. Currency benefit cited at about 6-8%.
Interest cost not expected to rise further and should decline as debt is retired; D&A expected to remain near Q2 levels.
Pertuzumab: Brazil PDP supplies start Q4 FY27 ($400m 10-year TCV); EU opens Q4 FY27; US launch from Q3 calendar 2028 (FY28 timing).
capex_capacity: Second fill-finish line for insulin commissioned in Malaysia; EMA and UK MHRA approvals secured for the new Insulin Glargine line, with Aspart supplies to Europe starting Q2 FY27.
Additional insulin capacity coming online internal and via CMO network, with capacity expected to ease supply constraints for Glargine.
Management is cautious on adding Aspart commercial payers until capacity builds up; US Aspart opens in a few quarters.
Intangibles capitalisation for new launches and Malaysia line depreciation drive D&A; most product intangibles now capitalised, with 10-12 year useful lives.
demand_pricing: Insulin franchise is over $300m annual run rate (from sub-$100m earlier); management says demand exceeds supply for Glargine and competition is limited to originators.

US: over $100m of new contracts and payor wins covering majority of US population; Yesintek US share 34%, surpassing originator; Yesafili (aflibercept) early launch encouraging with >50% market access and a major GPO partnership.
Europe: about 20 tender awards in Italy, Spain, France and Denmark; launches of ustekinumab autoinjector, denosumab and aflibercept.
Bevacizumab and denosumab share growth in US Part B is gradual, with management prioritising price and profitability over share; lowest price does not guarantee volume.
Management noted Part D erosion is steeper and Part B competition is intensifying, but insulin pricing is stable given limited competition.
Semaglutide: management stated Biocon has both synthetic and fermentation routes; fermentation seen as a cost advantage for oral forms.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $100m of new US contracts renewals or fresh revenue from H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Shreehas Tambe said it reflects new product launches, led by Yesintek, with share at 34% in the US; new launches are starting to show in the numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Size and timing of the one-off revenue deferral?
qa_highlights.answer: Kedar Upadhye said the deferral is about 5% of the quarter's revenue, mainly insulin and mAbs, shifting from September to October; normal cutoffs are about 1%. Shipping costs were deferred to Q3, while the rest of the opex stayed in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Q2 ex-R&D EBITDA margins lower, and what is the H2 margin view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 margins are distorted by the one-off shift. Full-year margin guidance is maintained, with H2 inventory build-up ahead of growth in aflibercept, aspart, ustekinumab and pertuzumab.

qa_highlights.question: Interest and D&A trend for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest cost was up INR10-20 crore QoQ on currency and working capital, not expected to rise further and to fall as debt is retired. D&A should stay around Q2 levels, with large changes unlikely.

qa_highlights.question: Crude-linked cost pressure in Generics?
qa_highlights.answer: In H1, higher freight cost about $5m and higher solvent cost about $5m, both absorbed in margins; management expects these to ease over the coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Quantified biosimilar scale-up over the next 12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Shreehas Tambe pointed to 9% H1 growth, a stronger H2, and double-digit annualised growth in recent years as the focus; Kedar Upadhye cited a currency benefit of about 6-8%.

risks_watch: Revenue timing: whether the ~5% (~$20m) deferred revenue and related EBITDA land in Q3 as guided.
H2 delivery against the stronger H2 and double-digit dollar growth promise, given H1 biosimilar growth of 9%.
Syngene: continued reduced demand from a large biologics client during FY27.
Yesafili and other new launches face rising competition and innovator patient-switching; US Part B price erosion and limited visibility from payers and innovators.
Logistics and geopolitical disruption affecting shipments; insulin capacity ramp timing for US Aspart.
Working capital build-up for launches, and whether debt reduction continues to lower interest cost.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H2 recovery and launch momentum, but cautious and defensive on Q2 numbers, explaining the one-off deferral and declining to give product-level or customer-level detail on launches and US Part B share.
key_quotes: We witnessed a one-off deferral in revenue recognition on certain biosimilar shipments this quarter on account of logistics issues, including those related to the ongoing geopolitical situation.
The underlying business remains strong, and we expect the second half of this fiscal to be stronger than the first half, as we have indicated earlier.
Insulin is a space that is very unique for Biocon. It is a very limited competition space. It is just the innovators and us.
The focus has always been for us to be profitable rather than just chase market share.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR7 crore, 1% margin in Q2 FY26

adds.what: Second fill-finish line for insulin commissioned in Malaysia
New Insulin Glargine line (EMA and UK MHRA approved); Aspart supplies to Europe starting Q2 FY27
Additional insulin capacity coming online internally and via CMO network

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 stronger than H1 with strong double-digit USD growth in biosimilars, backed by commissioned Malaysia insulin fill-finish line, approved Glargine line, $100m+ US contracts and Pertuzumab Brazil supplies from Q4 FY27, though ~5% of Q2 revenue slipped into October and no quantified full-year revenue growth was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Full-year biosimilar EBITDA margin guided to about 25% and mid-20s held; Generics margin recovered to 8% in Q2 from 1% a year ago, with freight and solvent cost pressure (~$5m each in H1) expected to ease.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Malaysia second insulin fill-finish line commissioned, Glargine line approved with Aspart Europe supplies starting Q2 FY27, and more insulin capacity coming online internally and via CMO; insulin franchise over $300m run rate with demand exceeding supply for Glargine.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 stronger than H1 with strong double-digit USD growth in biosimilars, versus H1 biosimilar revenue growth of 9%, aided by ~5% (~$20m) deferred revenue landing in October and $100m+ new US contracts.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No explicit new capex plan or utilisation figure was given; capacity additions are already commissioned or under construction, so a fresh announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Full-year margin guidance was only maintained, and H1 biosimilar growth of 9% sits well below the implied double-digit H2 USD growth, so an upgrade looks unlikely until H2 delivery is visible.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 delivery depends on ~5% (~$20m, roughly INR135-138 crore) deferred revenue landing in Q3, Syngene remains in transition with reduced biologics-client demand, and US Part B and Part D pricing erosion is steepening.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pertuzumab Brazil PDP supplies start Q4 FY27 ($400m 10-year TCV), EU opens Q4 FY27, US launch from Q3 calendar 2028; aflibercept, ustekinumab, denosumab and Aspart launches are ongoing.

rows.label: Insulin and Yesafili US contract wins
rows.why: Over $100m of new US contracts and payor wins covering most of the US population, Yesintek US share at 34%, and Yesafili with more than 50% market access plus a major GPO partnership.

rows.label: Interest cost decline as debt retired
rows.why: Interest cost fell 12% YoY to INR240 crore in Q2 and management says it will not rise further and should fall as debt is retired, with D&A near Q2 levels.

rows.label: H2 inventory build for launches
rows.why: Management flagged H2 inventory build-up ahead of growth in aflibercept, aspart, ustekinumab and pertuzumab, which adds working-capital needs.

tone.note: Management was confident on the H2 recovery, launch momentum and insulin supply, but defensive on Q2 numbers and the one-off deferral and declined product-level detail on US Part B share; analysts pressed on the size and timing of the deferral and the H2 delivery gap versus H1 growth of 9%.
